newsitem.title: RUSSIA: RUSSIA RTS NEEDS GOVERNMENT ORDER TO TRADE GAZPROM.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIA RTS NEEDS GOVERNMENT ORDER TO TRADE GAZPROM.

text.p: The head of Russia's capital markets watchdog said on Wednesday only the government could decide if the main equities market, the Russian Trading System (RTS), could once again trade Gazprom shares.

Shares in the natural gas monopoly ceased trading on the electronic over-the-counter RTS in early July after a government order named only four regional stock exchanges which would be allowed to sell the shares after July 1.
"That's a government-level decision," Dmitry Vasilyev, chairman of the Federal Commission for the Securities Market (FCSM), told a news conference.
"If the government decides to cancel the order then Gazprom can trade on the RTS and possibly on other exchanges. We don't have any major objections to it trading on the RTS as well."

The RTS, organised by the NAUFOR brokers association, currently trades 101 shares, including preferred stocks, plus a further 120 on its RTS-2 segment for less liquid shares. The RTS index of 21 leading shares is one of Russia's most widely watched equity indicators.
RTS president Dmitry Ponomaryov said on Tuesday the system was seeking to bring back Gazprom, which before the order racked up one of the highest daily turnovers for an individual share on the RTS.
Vasilyev said he did not know if the government planned to amend its order.
He expressed concern over the the shares' performance on the regional exchanges, joining Gazprom chief executive Rem Vyakhirev, who said last week the company would address the problem.

"Both the commission and Gazprom management are focusing most of their attention on improving the system of trading existing on the exchanges, particularly on the Moscow Stock Exchange," Vasilyev said.
"Neither I nor Mr Vyakhirev can be satisfied with the volume of trade and the range of deals."

Only two of the four exchanges named in the government order -- the Moscow Stock Exchange and the St Petersburg Stock Exchange -- have so far started trading Gazprom, an FCSM spokesman told Reuters on Tuesday.
